reason: The effective date and the 'up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations' match the notice. But the parenthetical implies the market-cap/AUM threshold alone defines a qualifying security. The notice requires all four criteria: monthly options volume over 10 million sides, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, Penny Interval Program participation, and the cap/AUM test. Eligibility is reviewed quarterly, and no expiry is listed on a day the issuer reports earnings after the close. found: A Qualifying Security is an individual stock or ETF that meets all of the following on the last trading day of the prior calendar quarter: Market capitalization greater than $700 billion for individual stocks based on the closing price, or AUM greater than $50 billion for ETFs based on NAV. Monthly options volume greater than 10 million sides in the month preceding quarter-end. Position limit of at least 250,000 contracts. Participates in the Penny Interval Program.
suggested_fix: Since 26 January 2026, Cboe has listed up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations on qualifying single stocks and ETFs. To qualify, a security must meet all of: market cap over $700bn (stocks) or AUM over $50bn (ETFs), monthly options volume over 10 million sides, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and Penny Interval Program participation. Eligibility is reviewed quarterly, and the Q1 2026 list was TSLA, NVDA, AAPL, IBIT, AMZN, META, AVGO, GOOGL and MSFT. These are not daily expirations.
